cues: In nineteen sixty five Sacks arrived in New York, in a horrid, pokey little apartment with nowhere to write.
He wrote part of his first book balanced on top of the refrigerator.
He longed for space, and found it in the library of the Albert Einstein College of Medicine, where he worked: a large table to write at, and stacks to wander with no idea what his eye might fall on.
That is serendipity: the joy of finding something valuable by accident.
